result.stack:
NO BUILD TOOLING AT ALL. No bundler, no transpiler, no framework, no CSS preprocessor, no TypeScript, no test framework package.

- Runtime: Node >= 22, `"type": "module"`, plain ESM `.mjs` everywhere on the server.
- Exactly ONE npm dependency in the whole project: `"chess.js": "1.4.0"`. Zero devDependencies. Tests run on the built-in `node --test`.
- Server: raw `node:http` + a hand-written 9-route router (src/server/http.mjs), a hand-written static file server (src/server/static.mjs) and a hand-written SSE hub (src/server/sse.mjs). Comment at the top of http.mjs: "Маршрутизатор на node:http. Никаких фреймворков — маршрутов девять."
- Client: three plain ES modules loaded with `<script type="module" src="/app.js">`, no imports from any CDN, no npm packages on the front end. `public/app.js` uses top-level `await` (it is a module).
- Rendering: NOT canvas. NOT React. Plain DOM + CSS transforms + inline SVG generated in JS. Board = 64 permanent `<div class="sq">` in a CSS grid + a separate absolutely-positioned `.pieces` layer where each piece is a `<div class="piece">` moved by `transform: translate(%,%)`.
- Transport: one GET /api/state + one SSE stream GET /api/events + five POST endpoints. No WebSocket.
- External engine: official Stockfish binary, downloaded at setup time into %LOCALAPPDATA%, driven as a SEPARATE PROCESS over UCI (deliberate weak coupling for GPL reasons). Not bundled, not in the repo.
- Zero external assets: no image files, no font files, no audio files, no icon files. The favicon is an inline `data:image/svg+xml` in index.html.
- package.json scripts: setup / start / test / test:unit / test:real / selfplay / audit / e2e / mirror / bench.
- .npmrc pins the npm cache to C: (`cache=C:\Users\user\AppData\Local\npm-cache`, `fund=false`, `audit=false`).

result.aesthetic:
"Ship's terminal": green phosphor vs amber phosphor on near-black, scanlines, vignette, brightness flicker. Every pixel is CSS or generated SVG — comment at the top of theme.css: "Всё рисуется CSS — ни одной картинки, ни одного внешнего шрифта."

PALETTE (public/theme.css :root, exact hex):
  --phosphor:       #7dff9b   green phosphor = side 1 (marines / white)
  --phosphor-dim:   #3d8a52   secondary text, borders on buttons
  --phosphor-faint: #1c3d27   tertiary text, coordinates, "nothing here yet"
  --amber:          #ffb347   amber phosphor = side 2 (xenos / black), all warnings
  --amber-dim:      #8a5f26
  --alert:          #ff4d4d   only for the broken-link dot
  --bg:             #050a06   page ground
  --panel:          #0a140c   panel fill
  --panel-edge:     #16301c   every 1px border, every separator
  --light-square:   #17301d
  --dark-square:    #0d1e11
Literal one-off colors: check square background #3a0f0f; eval-bar label text #dfffe8 on
rgba(5,10,6,0.78); overlay scrim rgba(5,10,6,0.9); glow shadows are
rgba(125,255,155,0.x) for green and rgba(255,179,71,0.x) for amber.

SPRITE PALETTE (public/sprites.js, per side, 4 colors each):
  w: { x:'#06170c'  outline, '#':'#7dff9b' body, o:'#dcffe6' highlight, '*':'#ffd166' accent }
  b: { x:'#1d0f00'  outline, '#':'#ffb347' body, o:'#ffe3ba' highlight, '*':'#b6ff5a' accent }
Doctrine stated in the file: the two sides differ by HUE, not by brightness, so they stay
legible on a dim CRT — and both hues are real period monitor phosphors.

FONT: `--font: 'Consolas', 'DejaVu Sans Mono', 'Courier New', monospace;` — system mono
only, no webfont, no @font-face, nothing loaded from Google Fonts. Body 14px,
`letter-spacing: 0.04em`. Titles are wide-tracked uppercase: `.title` 17px/0.22em,
`.start-title` 25px/0.3em, panel `<h2>` 11px/0.2em, buttons 12px/0.12em.
Text-shadow glow on titles only: `0 0 8px rgba(125,255,155,0.5)` / `0 0 14px …0.45`.

SPRITE TECHNIQUE (this is the signature move, copy it verbatim):
16 rows x 16 chars of ASCII, one string per row, 4 symbols: `.` transparent, `x` outline,
`#` body, `o` highlight, `*` accent. `spriteSvg()` walks each row, run-length-merges
horizontally identical pixels into one `<rect>`, and emits
`<svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" shape-rendering="crispEdges" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet">`.
Results are memoized in a `Map` keyed `set:color:type`. The RLE is not decoration — the
comment says without it the board would cost >4000 DOM nodes in pieces alone.
Two full sets exist: `classic` (traditional silhouettes) and `xeno` (marines vs xenomorphs),
switchable at runtime from the settings drawer.

RESOLUTION / SCALING: there is no fixed canvas. Board is `--board-max: min(72vh, 560px)`
(mobile: `min(92vw, 520px)`), squares are a `repeat(8,1fr)` grid, each piece is
`width:12.5%; height:12.5%` with `.piece svg { padding: 7%; image-rendering: pixelated }`.
So a 16x16 bitmap renders at ~65px and stays crisp via crispEdges + pixelated.

CRT EFFECT — one pseudo-element over everything, click-through:
  body::after { position:fixed; inset:0; pointer-events:none; z-index:100;
    background:
      repeating-linear-gradient(to bottom, rgba(0,0,0,.22) 0 1px, transparent 1px 3px),
      radial-gradient(ellipse at center, transparent 55%, rgba(0,0,0,.55) 100%);
    animation: flicker 5.5s infinite steps(60); }
`steps(60)` is what makes the flicker read as a CRT and not as a fade. The flicker
keyframes only dip at 97%/99% (0.93 / 0.96) — subtle, never distracting.

MOTION VOCABULARY (exact durations — reuse these numbers, they are tuned):
  piece move          transform 180ms ease-out (piece never re-created, only translated)
  drop landing        340ms cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1), starts 44px above with
                      scale(1.7) and opacity 0 — overshoot reads as a LANDING
  shockwave ring      460ms ease-out, scale(0.2)->2.2, opacity .7->0, amber border
  banner slide        translateY(-100%) -> 0, 220ms ease-out
  drawer slide        translateX(100%) -> 0, 200ms ease-out
  eval bar            height/width 260ms ease-out
  toast               opacity+translateY 200ms, auto-hides after 3400ms
  die shake           90ms infinite ±1px/±4deg; spin redraws every 70ms for 700ms
  boot typewriter     9ms per character, 120ms per line break
`@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` appears THREE times and kills the flicker, the
piece transition, the landing animation and the shockwave. Non-negotiable for parity.

LAYOUT: one CSS grid with named areas —
  grid-template-areas: 'head head head' / 'evalbar board side' / 'foot foot foot'
  grid-template-columns: 42px var(--board-max) minmax(300px, 1fr)
  max-width 1240px, `overflow:hidden` on html/body (desktop), gap 12px, padding 10px 14px.
At `max-width: 980px` it collapses to a single column, areas reorder to
'head' 'evalbar' 'board' 'foot' 'side', and the vertical eval bar becomes a horizontal
22px strip whose gradient direction flips. Note the file ends with a DUPLICATED narrow
media block and an explicit comment explaining that a later `.foot { flex-wrap: nowrap }`
rule won on equal specificity, so the mobile rules had to be repeated last. That kind of
comment — the fix plus why — is the house style.

CHROME DETAILS worth copying: 1px `--panel-edge` borders on everything; panel headers are
11px 0.2em uppercase dim-green on a bordered strip; buttons are transparent with a dim
border and hover = 10% tint + 8px glow; segmented controls (`.seg`) collapse borders with
`border-right-width:0` except `:last-child`, and the active one gets
`inset 0 0 10px rgba(125,255,155,.18)`; dice are 3x3 CSS grids of 5px round `<i>` pips;
`.pips` uses `●●●○○` text characters for remaining rolls; separators in the move log are
`border-top: 1px dashed var(--amber-dim)` with the text `═══ ДЕСАНТ #3 ═══`.
result.audio:
THERE IS NO AUDIO. NONE. I grepped the entire project (both the G: mirror and the C: live copy) for AudioContext / createOscillator / webkitAudioContext / `new Audio(` / sound / звук / audio — zero matches. There is no audio engine, no chiptune player, no sound file, no mute toggle, no volume setting, no `<audio>` element, no gesture-unlock code.

This is the single biggest gap in the reference project and the clearest place where the second game can EXCEED the bar rather than merely match it. Do not go looking for a helper to copy — there is nothing. If the new game wants sound, it must be written from scratch.

Constraints the new audio code must respect to stay consistent with the project's doctrine:
1. Zero external assets and zero dependencies. That rules out sample files and audio libraries; it means WebAudio synthesis (oscillators + gain envelopes + a noise buffer) written by hand, the same way sprites are hand-generated rather than shipped as PNGs.
2. Autoplay policy: nostromo-gambit has an explicit first-click gate already available — the `#start-go` "▶ НАЧАТЬ ОПЕРАЦИЮ" button on the start screen is guaranteed to be a user gesture. That is where `new AudioContext()` should be created / resumed.
3. It must honour the same accessibility instinct as `prefers-reduced-motion`: an audio on/off checkbox belongs in the settings drawer next to "Показывать шкалу оценки", persisted through the same settings POST, and it must default in a way that never surprises.
4. Every sound needs a named, motivated trigger the same way every animation does — the existing event vocabulary gives the hook points for free: `move`, `drop:start`, `drop:progress`, `drop:done`, `drop:skipped`, `dice`, `thinking`, check, game over, boot typewriter keyclick.
5. Palette discipline translates to audio: two timbres for the two sides (green/amber), one alert timbre, nothing else — the same "two hues, not two brightnesses" logic.
result.architecture:
SHAPE: a local single-player-at-one-screen web app with an authoritative Node server. The client is deliberately stupid. Top of public/app.js, verbatim:

  // Клиент намеренно ничего не решает сам: легальность ходов, расписание десанта
  // и счёт жетонов живут на сервере и приходят готовыми. Здесь только три вещи —
  // отрисовка, ввод указателя и тайминги анимаций.

THERE IS NO GAME LOOP. No requestAnimationFrame, no setInterval tick, no fixed timestep,
no update()/draw() split anywhere in the project. The app is 100% event-driven: server
state changes -> SSE frame -> `applyState(next)` -> full re-render of a small DOM. All
motion is delegated to CSS transitions/animations. The only timers in the client are the
dice spin (`setInterval(…, 70)` for 700 ms), the boot typewriter (chained `setTimeout`),
the toast dismissal (3400 ms) and shockwave cleanup (500 ms). If the second game needs a
real-time loop, that pattern must be invented — there is nothing here to copy.

SERVER STATE MACHINE — `class Game` (src/game/game.mjs), 356 lines:
  phase: 'idle' | 'dropping' | 'over'   (set in #refreshGameOver)
  version: monotonically incremented on EVERY mutation; it is both the SSE event id and
           the optimistic-concurrency token.
  Own journal instead of the library's: `atoms[]` (each `{kind:'move'|'drop', …}`) plus a
  parallel `snapshots[]` stack of FENs. Reason is documented at the top of the file —
  chess.js 1.4.0 `load()` calls `clear()` and destroys its own history, and the drop
  mechanic must rebuild the position from FEN, so undo/move-list/threefold would have
  silently vanished. There is a regression test for exactly this.
  Stable piece identity: `this.pieces` is a Map square -> `{id:'p17', type, color}`.
  IDs are assigned from a module-level `nextPieceId` counter and are what makes the client
  animate instead of blink. `#applyPieceMove(m)` transfers the id using the SEMANTICS of
  the move (en-passant victim square, castling rook hop, promotion type swap) because you
  cannot infer identity by diffing two positions.
  Honest degradation: after undo, ids are re-issued (`#rebuildPieceIds`) and the board
  redraws wholesale, with a comment saying this is more honest than pretending.

APP ORCHESTRATOR — `class App` (src/server/main.mjs), 360 lines: owns sessionId (randomUUID),
Game, SseHub, EnginePool, AnalysisEngine, Rng, and the `dropInProgress` / `dropAbort` pair.
Async work (computer move, drop search) is deliberately NOT awaited inside the HTTP handler:

  // Намеренно не await: ход считается в фоне, а состояние уезжает клиенту событием.
  // Иначе HTTP-ответ на ход человека ждал бы, пока движок додумает свой…

and every background task re-checks `this.game.version !== versionAtStart` before applying
its result, because the game may have been reset/undone while it was thinking.

SCREENS (there are no routes; screens are stacked z-indexed overlays in one HTML file):
  .start   z-index 90  full-screen start card, `.off` hides it
  .drawer  z-index 60  settings, slides in from the right
  .overlay z-index 50  two of them: game-over card and promotion picker; `.on` shows
  .toast   z-index 70  transient message
  body::after z-index 100 CRT layer above everything, pointer-events none
The start screen is shown ONLY when there is nothing to resume — last 8 lines of app.js:
`const gameInProgress = state && (state.moveLog.length > 0 || state.dropLog.length > 0)`;
if resuming it shows the toast «ПАРТИЯ ВОССТАНОВЛЕНА» instead. This exists because a
reload mid-game used to cover a live board with a screen whose only button would erase it.

HTTP API (src/server/http.mjs): GET /api/state, GET /api/events, GET /health,
POST /api/move | /api/roll | /api/new-game | /api/undo | /api/settings,
POST /api/_test/fen (only when NODE_ENV=test). One `STATUS` table maps error codes to
HTTP statuses (409 for conflicts, 422 for illegal move, 503 for engine down). Body limit
64 KB. Errors are caught so a bad request never kills a game in progress.

OPTIMISTIC CONCURRENCY: client sends `version: state.version` with move/roll/undo; a
mismatch returns `{code:'STALE_VERSION'}` and the client treats it as non-error and just
re-reads state (`if (data.code === 'STALE_VERSION') { await refresh(); return data; }`).

EVENT STREAM: exactly ONE multiplexed SSE endpoint, with the reason spelled out — HTTP/1.1
allows ~6 connections per origin, two streams x two tabs already eats four. Event names:
`snapshot`, `state`, `move`, `settings` (all carry a full snapshot and an `id:`),
plus volatile `eval`, `thinking`, `drop:progress` (NO `id:`, so they cannot poison
Last-Event-ID), plus `dice`, `drop:start`, `drop:done`, `drop:skipped`.
A 200-frame ring buffer replays from Last-Event-ID; if there is a gap it falls back to a
full snapshot. 15 s heartbeat comments, `retry: 3000`, `setNoDelay(true)` (Nagle was
batching 60-byte eval frames into 40 ms jerks), `X-Accel-Buffering: no`, `no-transform`.

INPUT (public/board.js `#bindPointer`): Pointer Events only — NOT HTML5 drag&drop, with
the reason in a comment (ghost image, no touch support, no control over animation). Two
interaction modes on the same handler: drag (pointerdown -> capture -> pointermove sets
`transform` in px -> pointerup hit-tests) and click-click (select source, then click a
highlighted target). `#squareFromPoint(x,y)` converts client coords via
`getBoundingClientRect()` and a /8 floor. On release the piece is ALWAYS snapped back
locally and the server's echo is what actually moves it. `board.setLocked()` freezes input
during a drop and after game over. `.board { touch-action: none; user-select: none }`.
Keyboard: only `Escape` (closes drawer + promo, clears selection).

PERSISTENCE: there is none on the client — no localStorage, no cookies, no save file.
State lives in server memory; a page reload re-fetches it. Runtime artifacts (engine
binary, selfplay NDJSON, PID registry) live in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\nostromo-gambit\` via
src/shared/paths.mjs, deliberately NOT next to the sources, because the source folder is
on a Google Drive virtual volume. `writeJsonAtomic()` = write .tmp then rename.

DETERMINISM: `makeRng(seed)` (xorshift128+) everywhere; `Math.random` appears exactly once
in the whole client and only to spin the dice faces visually. Same seed reproduces the
whole game including the Fischer start position (`fischerFen(makeRng('fischer:'+seed))`).

result.tone:
VOICE. Two registers, held consistently. The interface speaks as a 1979 ship's computer: uppercase, clipped, factual, never cute, never emoji. The code comments and the docs speak as an engineer writing to a colleague: every non-obvious line carries WHY, usually with the evidence attached. Examples of the comment style, verbatim:
  "Указатель, а не нативный drag&drop: последний тащит призрачную картинку, не работает
   на касании и не даёт управлять анимацией."
  "Порядок важен: сначала позиция, потом класс анимации, иначе переменные --tx/--ty ещё
   не заданы и фигура прилетает в угол."
  "Логистическое отображение: линейное бесполезно, на нём интересный диапазон ±80 сп
   неразличим, а ±1500 упирается в край."
  "Печать по буквам — ради ощущения загрузки старой игры, не ради информации."
  "Честный отказ лучше подделанного десанта: жетон возвращается, а причина показывается
   игроку словами."
Notice the pattern: decision, then the rejected alternative, then the consequence. Copy it.

HONESTY AS A DESIGN PRINCIPLE. This is the strongest through-line and the thing that makes
the project feel expensive. When something cannot be done properly it is disabled and said
out loud, in the UI, not hidden: Fischer castling is off and the start screen says so;
a failed drop refunds the die and prints the reason; a widened tolerance is written into
the drop log as «ДОПУСК РАСШИРЕН ДО ±45 СП»; undo after a drop admits it must redraw the
whole board. README and REPORT both end with «Известные ограничения» / «Что осталось
несделанным». The second game must have that section too.

OPENING. Not a splash screen — a configuration terminal, exactly like an era game. The
boot text types itself character by character (9 ms/char, 120 ms/line) above the title,
then a single card asks EVERYTHING at once via segmented buttons: player 1 human/computer,
player 2 human/computer, computer level 1–5, planner, start position, dice rolls per
player, auto-drop frequency. Every option has a live one-line explanatory note under it
(`.opt-note`, amber-dim) that changes as you select — the level note, the planner blurb,
the Fischer caveat. One amber call-to-action: «▶ НАЧАТЬ ОПЕРАЦИЮ». Under it, one honest
line about the 32-piece ceiling.

DIFFICULTY. Five named levels with character, not numbers: 1 РЯДОВОЙ / 2 КАПРАЛ /
3 СЕРЖАНТ / 4 ЛЕЙТЕНАНТ / 5 MU-TH-UR 6000 («Полная сила на этой машине. Удачи.»).
Default is 3. Crucially, weakening is done by MultiPV move selection within a `slackCp`
window (220/130/60/20/0), NOT by cutting depth — with the stated reason: a depth-starved
engine plays *stranger*, not weaker; it still never blunders two-move tactics but stops
having a plan. Even level 1 is forbidden from gifting a queen.

PACING. Turn-based, no timers, no pressure. The drama is manufactured in two places:
(1) the drop — a banner slides down over the board, the board dims to 0.55 and goes
`cursor:wait`, a phase-weighted progress bar advances through four named phases
(weights 0.05/0.2/0.55/1.0 so the bar never lies about which stage it is in), and it ends
with pieces falling from above with an overshoot plus amber shockwave rings and a toast;
(2) the dice — 700 ms of shaking, faces reshuffling every 70 ms, then the readout line
that tells you exactly what you bought. Search takes 4–6 s in practice and REPORT.md says
plainly that this was over the 2.5 s target — the progress bar with meaningful phase names
is the accepted mitigation: "ожидание читается как работа, а не как зависание."

WHAT MAKES IT FEEL GOOD. (a) Nothing ever blinks: stable piece ids mean every change is a
motion. (b) Every number shown is explained somewhere — the drop log prints
`+0.34 → +0.29 · Δ -5 сп · ЦЕЛЬ 0 · 4.2 с` and the header prints the hold count.
(c) Personality lives in tables, not in code branches — three "planners" (МАТЬ / БИШОП /
ЭШ, borrowed conceptually from RimWorld storytellers) differ only by weights and tolerance,
each with a `tone: { start, done, skipped }` string triple; ЭШ's line is
«ВЫСАДКА ВЫПОЛНЕНА. НЕ МОГУ ЛГАТЬ О ВАШИХ ШАНСАХ.». (d) Tension is built into the dice
math rather than into UI noise: sum buys tonnage, spread buys bias, and a double gives max
tonnage with ZERO bias while 6–1 gives max bias with almost no tonnage — you cannot have
both. (e) The one aesthetic ruling the user made mid-build is recorded in REPORT.md and
worth internalizing: the eval bar used to be "green vs empty", which speaks the language of
white and black; it was recolored to green-vs-amber so it speaks the language of THIS
game's two sides.

ENDING. A centered card over a 0.9 scrim: the reason in huge tracked caps («МАТ»), one
statistics line («Ходов: 47 · Десантов: 6 · Фигур на доске: 21»), and two buttons —
«НОВАЯ ПАРТИЯ» (returns to the configuration terminal, never straight into a game) and
«ПОСМОТРЕТЬ ПАРТИЮ» (dismisses the card so you can study the final position). There is also
`Game.toPgn()` which exports the game with drops as PGN comments, so a game can be re-read.
result.how_to_run:
DEVELOPMENT LOCATION IS A HARD CONSTRAINT — read this before writing a line of the new game.
G:\Другие компьютеры\PAULEKMAN\dev is a Google Drive virtual volume. Verified in REPORT.md:
`npm install` there produces ZERO-LENGTH files (npm swallows TAR_ENTRY_ERROR and continues,
so chess.js "installed successfully" with every file empty and imports failed with
"Invalid package config"); junctions cannot be created ("требуется локальный том NTFS");
filesystem watch events are lost. Own writes do go through fine.
Therefore: build and run in C:\dev\<project>, and mirror sources to G: with a script like
scripts/mirror-to-drive.mjs, which verifies each copied file's size matches and exits 1 on
mismatch. Do the same for the second game.

Commands (from C:\dev\nostromo-gambit):
  npm install                     one dep, chess.js
  npm run setup                   downloads official Stockfish (~81 MB), verifies sha256
                                  from the GitHub API, unpacks to
                                  %LOCALAPPDATA%\nostromo-gambit\engine\, probes UCI and
                                  benchmarks nps. Idempotent.
  npm start                       node src/server/main.mjs
  open http://127.0.0.1:7777      HOST/PORT overridable via env (default 127.0.0.1:7777)
  ENGINE=mock npm start           runs with the in-process MockEngine, no Stockfish needed
  npm test                        118 tests, node --test, ~14 s
  npm run selfplay -- --games=5 --workers=2      the project's main oracle: self-play with
                                  invariants checked on EVERY ply; NDJSON output to
                                  %LOCALAPPDATA%\nostromo-gambit\selfplay\
  npm run bench -- --positions=12 --storyteller=all
  npm run e2e                     serves for browser-driven checking
  npm run mirror                  C: -> G: source mirror

Startup console output is Russian and reports the engine name/kind, the pool size and
aggregate Mnps, then the URL. Shutdown handles SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP/SIGBREAK, plus a
synchronous `process.on('exit')` last resort that kills engine child processes, plus a
PID registry that reaps engines orphaned by previous runs (closed terminal windows / Task
Manager kills give no chance for a clean stop).

DEPLOYMENT: none. No artifact URL, no itch.io, no GitHub Pages, no Docker, no CI. It is a
localhost-only, single-screen Node app. README notes multiplayer would be additive (state
already lives on the server) but is not implemented. NOTE for the second game: if it can be
made a self-contained single-file HTML page with no server, it can be published as an
Artifact and the user gets a link — that is a real upgrade over this project's ergonomics,
and nothing in the aesthetic depends on the server. The server exists here only because
Stockfish is a native process.

TESTING DOCTRINE (worth matching): the fast tier (101 unit tests) runs entirely against an
in-process MockEngine so it stays in seconds — "иначе его перестали бы гонять". Real
Stockfish is used only where it proves something the mock cannot: the wire protocol,
process lifecycle, absence of orphans, and actual drop quality. Integration tests boot the
real server on port 0 (so parallel test files don't fight over a port) and parse raw SSE
frames by hand rather than using EventSource, because the frame format is what's under test.

result: # JUICE DIRECTION — «ПРОТОКОЛ ГЕЛЛЕРА» *(alt title: «14 000 605». Subtitle: МОРСКОЙ БОЙ В МУЛЬТИВСЕЛЕННОЙ · ТАКТИЧЕСКИЙ МОДУЛЬ)* ## 0. The one architectural break from the reference, and why nostromo-gambit has **no rAF loop and no canvas** — every motion is a CSS transition on a stable-id DOM node. That works because chess has ≤32 entities that move once per second. Here the enemy grid must draw ~8 overlapping translucent fleet silhouettes *plus* a 100-cell dithered probability field, reshuffling continuously. That is 500+ draw ops per frame. DOM cannot do it, and CSS cannot express additive blending. **Decision: hybrid.** Chrome (header, HUD panels, counter, logs, drawer, overlays, toast, CRT layer) stays DOM + `theme.css`, lifted verbatim. Only the two grids become ``, with one shared `requestAnimationFrame` loop. Comment to write at the top of `render.mjs`: ```js // Единственный rAF во всём проекте. В «Ностромо» цикла не было и не требовалось: // там тридцать две сущности двигались раз в секунду и CSS справлялся сам. // Здесь на вражеской сетке кипит восемь наложенных силуэтов и поле вероятностей // из ста ячеек — это пятьсот операций рисования на кадр. DOM столько не тянет, // а сложение прозрачностей ('lighter') в CSS не выражается вовсе. ``` **Canvas resolution: 160×160 internal per board** (10×10 cells × 16 px — the same 16 px module as the reference sprites). Scaled by an **integer** factor only: `scale = Math.max(1, Math.floor(cssPx / 160))`, `ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled = false`, `image-rendering: pixelated`. At 480 px CSS that is ×3. Never a fractional scale — half-pixels are how 8-bit dies. --- ## 1. GHOST FLEET — the draw algorithm Two layers, drawn bottom-up into the same canvas each frame. ### 1a. Probability field, as a 4×4 ordered dither (this is the signature move) The server sends a quantized occupancy field: `Uint8Array(100)`, value 0–16 = "in how many sixteenths of sampled realities is this cell occupied". Not an alpha ramp — **a count of lit sub-pixels**. Each 16×16 cell is subdivided into a 4×4 grid of 4×4-px blocks. A standard Bayer matrix decides which blocks are lit: ```js const BAYER4 = [ 0, 8, 2,10, 12, 4,14, 6, 3,11, 1, 9, 15, 7,13, 5]; // уровень L (0..16): блок i горит, если BAYER4[i] < L ``` Precompute **17 offscreen 16×16 tiles per hue** at load (`buildDitherTiles(hex)` → `OffscreenCanvas[17]`). Per frame the field costs exactly 100 `drawImage` calls. Zero per-pixel work. Why dither and not alpha: an alpha ramp at p=0.08 is a flat dim grey square and reads as *fog*. A 1-of-16 dither is a single lit 4×4 pixel in a black cell and reads as *a possibility*. It is also literally how an NES would have done it. ### 1b. Ghost silhouettes — additive, slot-staggered, held for 3 frames ```js const GHOST_SLOTS = 8; // сколько силуэтов живёт одновременно const SLOT_PERIOD = 24; // кадров жизни одного силуэта (400 мс) const SLOT_STAGGER = 7; // сдвиг фаз между слотами (24 и 7 взаимно просты) const GHOST_ALPHA = 0.075; // на один силуэт, режим 'lighter' ``` Each frame: `for (let i = 0; i < 8; i++) if ((frame + i * SLOT_STAGGER) % SLOT_PERIOD === 0) slot[i] = pool.take();` — one replacement roughly every 3 frames, never all at once. The eye reads staggered 400 ms lifetimes as **boiling**; it reads a global 60 Hz reshuffle as **TV static**. This distinction is the entire difference between "delicious" and "unreadable". Then: ```js ctx.globalCompositeOperation = 'lighter'; for (const g of slot) { ctx.globalAlpha = GHOST_ALPHA * g.fade; // fade: 0→1 за 4 кадра, 1→0 за 4 кадра ctx.fillStyle = WARP_RGB; for (const run of g.runs) ctx.fillRect(run.x*16 + g.jx, run.y*16 + g.jy, run.w*16, 16); } ctx.globalCompositeOperation = 'source-over'; ``` `g.runs` is the sample's occupancy bitmask **run-length-merged horizontally**, exactly the trick `sprites.js` uses to avoid 4000 DOM nodes: a 5-cell ship is one `fillRect`, not five. `g.jx/g.jy` is a ±1 px jitter chosen **once when the slot is filled**, not per frame — per-frame jitter is noise, per-ghost jitter is texture. **Convergence is free and needs no extra code.** Additive blending means a cell present in 1 of 8 ghosts sits at α 0.075 (barely there); a cell present in all 8 sits at α 0.6 and reads as a solid hull. As the possibility space collapses, samples agree, sums saturate, and the fleet *materialises out of its own agreement*. Nothing fades in. The ghosts simply start telling the same story. Write that in a comment. **Boil rate is a variable.** `SLOT_PERIOD` drops to 4 frames for 300 ms after any shot (`ВСКИПАНИЕ` — the possibility space visibly re-thinks), then eases back over 500 ms via `slotPeriod = 4 + 20 * ease(t)`. Reduced motion: `SLOT_SLOTS = 0`, draw the mean field only, statically. --- ## 2. THE REALITIES COUNTER Centre column, between the two boards, because it is physically between the two realities. `34px`, `letter-spacing: 0.18em`, 8 digit cells + thin-space group separators: `≈ 14 000 605`. **Honesty rule, borrowed from the reference's doctrine:** the exact count is #P-hard in general. The server counts exactly by DFS with pruning while the search stays under a `2e6`-node budget; above that it Monte-Carlo estimates. The estimate is prefixed `≈` and rendered in `--warp`. The moment the count becomes exact the tilde disappears and the digits shift to `--bone`. **The counter visibly stops lying at you.** That transition (usually around 10⁴) is one of the best beats in the game and it costs one CSS class. Odometer: each digit is a `0..9`, `overflow:hidden`, height 34px, the `` is a 10-glyph vertical strip translated by `translateY(-value * 34px)`, `transition: transform 260ms cubic-bezier(0.34,1.56,0.64,1)` — the same overshoot curve as the landing animation, so the whole project speaks one motion language. Stagger `transition-delay: 18ms * (7 - index)` so the change ripples right-to-left. **COLLAPSE BEAT** — fires when `next < prev / 4`: 1. **Freeze frame, 90 ms.** The rAF loop early-returns; the last frame stays on screen. Music gain → 0.3 in 20 ms. 2. **Scramble, 400 ms.** Every digit that will change cycles random glyphs at 40 ms. 3. **Shake, 220 ms.** The `.app` gets `transform: translate(var(--sx), var(--sy))` driven by the loop: amplitude 5 px, three oscillations, decaying linearly, snapped to integer pixels. 4. Ghost layer drawn **twice** for 6 frames, at `(+1,0)` in `--warp` and `(-1,0)` in `--pinned` — an 8-bit chromatic split, not a shader. 5. Digits land. SFX: the 5-blip descending arpeggio (§7). Reduced motion: no freeze, no shake, no scramble; digits snap. --- ## 3. MISS / HIT / KILL — three escalating beats ### МИМО — a constraint, not nothing (the hardest one to get right) The point of the whole game is that a miss *destroys realities*. So make the destruction the animation, not the water splash. - The cell locks instantly to the **pinned-void tile**: `--void-hard #0a1418` fill, 1 px inset `--pinned-dim` border, a 2×2-px ✕ in `--pinned-dim` at the centre. Hard, cold, permanent. It never boils again. - **Culling, 180 ms.** Every ghost currently on screen that contained that cell is re-drawn in `--alert` at α 0.5 and **dissolves**: three steps at 60 ms, each dropping a random 35 % of its remaining 4×4 blocks (seeded from the deterministic `Rng` so replays match). You watch a hundred thousand futures come apart into red dust. - The counter drops. Ledger panel gets a line: `D4 · ПУСТО · −812 340 РЕАЛЬНОСТЕЙ`. **Every miss prints its own body count.** That number is the reward. A miss in this game should feel like a good move, and it will, because you can read exactly how much of the multiverse it cost the enemy. - SFX: dry bandpassed noise thud + a high 18 ms tick — the tick is the sound of *information being recorded*. ### ПОПАЛ - 2-frame full-board white flash: `--bone` at α 0.12 over everything, `'lighter'`. - The cell goes solid `--amber`. An expanding **square** ring: 1-cell outline growing one cell per 4 frames for 3 steps, each step dithered one level dimmer (16 → 10 → 5 → 0). Squares, not circles — the reference's round `.shock` belongs to CSS; on a 16 px pixel grid a square ring is more honest and reads better. - `ВСКИПАНИЕ`: boil rate to 4 frames for 300 ms while the sampler re-conditions. The possibility space visibly *lurches*. - Counter dive, usually a collapse beat. ### УБИТ — the full ceremony 1. 90 ms freeze frame. 2. The entire ship resolves at once: drawn from the real 16 px ship sprite set (RLE'd, same authoring format as `sprites.js`), full brightness, outline forced to `--bone` for 120 ms. 3. Screen shake 5 px / 3 oscillations / 220 ms. 4. **Hull burn, 700 ms**: hull pixels flip to `*` accent then to void, sweeping top-to-bottom one 4 px row per 40 ms. 5. Toast «КОРПУС РАЗРУШЕН · ЭСМИНЕЦ (3)». Ledger line. The largest counter dive of the game — killing a ship removes an entire degree of freedom, and the counter shows it. 6. Audio ducks to 0.35× for 600 ms. Escalation in one sentence, which is how it should be tuned: **miss = cold click + red dust; hit = white flash + boil; kill = freeze + shake + burn + the big number falling.** --- ## 4. PINNING REALITY — the Geller field Player action on **their own** board (which also boils — your fleet is undetermined too, and the machine does that combinatorics for you, per the seed idea). Spend one charge, select a 3×3 region: your ships inside it may never be moved by a future evasion again. Animation, 500 ms: - A **Bresenham circle** expands from the centre cell, 3 concentric 1-px rings, radius growing 16 px per 80 ms, drawn in `--pinned`. - As the ring passes over each cell, that cell's dither level is **quantised to 0 or 16**. Nothing in between. This is the whole idea made visible: *inside the field, probability has only two values.* - Per-cell jitter goes to 0 inside the bubble. The boil stops dead. Motion outside, stillness inside — the contrast is the payoff. - Hue switch violet → ice-cyan. - Border afterwards: 1 px dotted `--pinned` marching ants, offset cycling 0-1-2-3 at **8 fps** (four discrete steps, not a smooth CSS animation — 8-bit means quantised time too). - SFX: two sines rising 220→660 Hz whose mutual detune goes 40 cents → 0 over 420 ms, terminated by a hard 25 ms square click. The sound of two realities becoming one, then sealed. Charges shown as `●●○` pips in `--pinned`, reusing the existing `.pips` rule. --- ## 5. SCREEN LAYOUT Two boards, HUD between them. ```css .app { grid-template-columns: var(--board-max) minmax(280px, 1fr) var(--board-max); grid-template-areas: 'head head head' 'enemy hud own' 'foot foot foot'; } :root { --board-max: min(46vh, 480px); } /* 480 + 280 + 480 = 1240 — тот же предел */ ``` - **Left, `enemy`** — ВРАЖЕСКИЙ СЕКТОР. Where you shoot. Where the ghosts live. Panel header amber. - **Centre, `hud`** — top to bottom: the realities counter (the visual centre of the whole game), `ЖУРНАЛ ОГРАНИЧЕНИЙ` (every answer given, `D4 · ПУСТО · −812 340`), Geller charges, the multi-branch munition, `ЖУРНАЛ`. - **Right, `own`** — ВАШ ФЛОТ. Your own boil, your pinned regions. Panel header green. Collapse at `max-width: 1100px` to one column, order `head / hud / enemy / own / foot` — the counter goes **first** on mobile, because it is the game. Board canvases sit in a `.board-wrap` with the existing 1 px `--panel-edge` border, coordinate labels in `--phosphor-faint` outside the canvas as DOM (crisp Cyrillic beats blitted text). Input: Pointer Events, `#cellFromPoint(x,y)` = `getBoundingClientRect()` + `/10` floor — the same shape as `board.js`'s `#squareFromPoint`, minus drag. --- ## 6. PALETTE Five hues, each one a proposition: **green = what is true · violet = what is not yet decided · cyan = what you have forbidden to change · amber = the enemy · red = what you destroyed.** ```css :root { --void: #04060c; /* глубже и синее, чем #050a06 — это уже не корабль, это варп */ --panel: #0a0f1a; --panel-edge: #1a2340; --grid-a: #0b1220; --grid-b: #070d18; --phosphor: #7dff9b; /* ваш флот, подтверждённая реальность */ --phosphor-dim: #3d8a52; --phosphor-faint:#1c3d27; --warp: #a05cff; /* неопределённость, призраки */ --warp-dim: #4a2585; --warp-faint: #1d1038; --pinned: #9fe8ff; /* поле Геллера, твёрдая холодная реальность */ --pinned-dim: #3d7b93; --void-hard: #0a1418; /* клетка, где точно ничего нет */ --amber: #ffb347; /* вражеский корпус, попадания */ --amber-dim: #8a5f26; --alert: #ff4d4d; /* вырезанные ветки */ --bone: #e8f0ff; /* максимальная яркость: вспышка, контур убитого */ } ``` Ship sprite palettes, same 4-key format as `sprites.js`: ```js export const PALETTES = { own: { x:'#06170c', '#':'#7dff9b', o:'#dcffe6', '*':'#9fe8ff' }, enemy: { x:'#1d0f00', '#':'#ffb347', o:'#ffe3ba', '*':'#ff4d4d' }, ghost: { x:'#1d1038', '#':'#a05cff', o:'#c9a0ff', '*':'#a05cff' }, }; ``` CRT layer kept verbatim, with the vignette pushed slightly darker (`rgba(0,0,0,.62)`) so the violet reads as glow rather than haze. --- ## 7. AUDIO — written from scratch, and it is where this game exceeds the bar `AudioContext` created inside the `«▶ НАЧАТЬ ОПЕРАЦИЮ»` click handler — the one guaranteed gesture, exactly as in the reference's start screen. Two settings in the drawer: `ЗВУК` and `МУЗЫКА`, persisted through the same settings POST. Chain: `voices → masterGain(0.35) → waveShaper(tanh, 1024) → warpFilter(lowpass) → destination`. Everything is driven by one number, `collapse ∈ [0,1]` = `1 - log(realities)/log(realitiesAtStart)`. **The music is the mechanic.** Four voices: | voice | recipe | driven by collapse | |---|---|---| | BASS | `square` 55–110 Hz, 2 ms attack / 180 ms decay, eighth notes | none (the anchor) | | PAD | **two** `sawtooth` on the same note, `detune = ±42 * (1 - collapse)` cents, plus a 0.17 Hz LFO on detune of depth `18 * (1 - collapse)` | **this is the whole design**: seasick chorus at 14 million, dead-clean unison at 1 | | LEAD | `triangle`, sparse 4-note A-minor motif, only while a shot is pending | — | | HISS | one 2 s white-noise buffer, looped, `bandpass` 2200 Hz Q 1.2, gain `0.02 * (1 - collapse)` | the sound of undetermined space; it goes *silent* as you pin reality | `warpFilter.frequency = 800 + 6000 * collapse` — the world literally gets clearer. Tempo 92 BPM + 8 × collapse. SFX (all synthesised, no buffers except the one noise source): - **ВЫСТРЕЛ** — `square` 880→110 Hz exp over 90 ms, gain 0.25→0.001; + 40 ms noise through highpass 1200. - **МИМО** — 60 ms noise, bandpass 400 Hz Q 6, gain 0.12; then `sine` 196 Hz 120 ms (a low, dry "no"); then `triangle` 1568 Hz **18 ms** — the information tick. - **ПОПАЛ** — `square` 220 + `square` 330 (a fifth), 160 ms, 8 ms attack; + 120 ms noise, lowpass 900→300. - **УБИТ** — (1) 90 ms of silence, (2) 700 ms noise, lowpass 4000→120 exp, gain 0.4, (3) `sawtooth` 330→41 Hz over 900 ms. Music ducks 0.35× for 600 ms, 40 ms ramps. - **КОЛЛАПС** — five `square` blips 28 ms apart, 40 ms each: 1318, 1046, 880, 659, 440 Hz. The final blip drops **one semitone per order of magnitude lost**. The odometer has a voice, and its pitch tells you how big the collapse was before you finish reading the digits. - **ПОЛЕ ГЕЛЛЕРА** — §4. - **СМЕЩЕНИЕ** (your fleet evades) — noise bandpass sweeping 300→3000 Hz over 240 ms, gain 0.10, + an upward pitch blip. It should feel *slightly guilty*: you fed the dark god. - **UI** — `square` 1200 Hz 12 ms gain 0.05. Boot typewriter: `square` 2000 Hz 6 ms gain 0.03, **every third character only** (every character is a machine gun). --- ## 8. TITLE, TRANSITIONS, ENDINGS **Title screen = attract mode = a live demo of the mechanic.** Behind the configuration card, the ghost renderer runs on a decorative 10×10 with **zero constraints**: maximum boil, full violet, and the counter showing the unconstrained total ticking as the sampler warms up. Boot typewriter above it (9 ms/char, 120 ms/line): ``` ВЫЧИСЛИТЕЛЬНЫЙ КОМПЛЕКС · ИНИЦИАЛИЗАЦИЯ ПРИВОД АЛЬКУБЬЕРРЕ .................. ХОЛОДНЫЙ ГЕНЕРАТОР ПОЛЯ ГЕЛЛЕРА .............. ЗАРЯЖЕН ПЕРЕСЧЁТ СОГЛАСОВАННЫХ РЕАЛЬНОСТЕЙ .. 14 000 605 ЗА ПРЕДЕЛАМИ ПОЛЯ НИЧТО НЕ ЗАКРЕПЛЕНО ``` Config card: segmented controls (`.seg`, lifted), each with a live `.opt-note`. Options: сетка 8/10/12, флот, СМЕЩЕНИЯ противника (никогда / раз в 3 хода / каждый ход — «каждый ход» note: «Честно предупреждаю: это очень тяжело»), зарядов Геллера, уровень (five named levels with character, per the reference's doctrine), сид. **Transition in:** boil freezes 200 ms → counter snaps to the true start count → a 6-step vertical **dither wipe** (Bayer threshold rising, 240 ms). Not a fade. Fades are 16-bit. **Поражение:** your last hull dies → your pinned cells **unpin one by one**, 80 ms apart (reverse Geller, cyan → violet), the palette drains green → violet over 1.2 s, HISS gain swells to 0.25, and the counter **runs upward** and keeps going past the screen width. Card: «ВЫ ПЕРЕСТАЛИ БЫТЬ ОПРЕДЕЛЁННЫМ» + stat line «Выстрелов: 63 · Смещений: 11 · Полей Геллера: 3». Buttons «НОВАЯ ОПЕРАЦИЯ» / «ПОСМОТРЕТЬ СЕКТОР» — never straight into a new game, same as the reference. **Победа:** last enemy ship dies → counter goes to **1**. The whole enemy board resolves in one 600 ms pass into solid amber hulls. HISS → 0, PAD detune → 0, one clean unison chord, and then **900 ms of the number `1` alone on a still screen** before the card slides in. That silence is the payoff of the entire game; do not shorten it. Card: «ОСТАЛАСЬ ОДНА РЕАЛЬНОСТЬ». --- ## 9. THREE SCREENSHOT MOMENTS 1. **Первый промах, который стоил миллиона.** Counter mid-collapse, 8 digits scrambling down to 6, red ghost-dust dissolving across half the board, freeze-frame held. 2. **Печать поля Геллера.** Left half of your fleet boiling violet, right half hard ice-cyan and perfectly still, with the dither boundary visible block by block. One image that explains the entire mechanic without a word. 3. **`1`.** Two fully solid fleets, no boil anywhere, and a single digit in `--bone` under the words ОСТАЛАСЬ ОДНА РЕАЛЬНОСТЬ. --- ## 10. PERFORMANCE BUDGET (why 60 fps is not in doubt) Per board per frame: 100 `drawImage` (pre-baked dither tiles, 17 levels × 4 hues = 68 offscreen 16×16 canvases built once at load) + 8 ghosts × ≤17 RLE runs ≈ 136 `fillRect` + ~20 ops of chrome. ≈ 260 ops; two boards ≈ 520. On a 160×160 backing store that is well under 2 ms. The rules: **never compute dither per pixel; never allocate in the loop; never call `getImageData`; ghost samples arrive pre-RLE'd as `Uint8Array` bitmasks and are decoded once when a slot takes them.** Timing is in **frames**, not milliseconds, with a delta guard that skips logic if `dt > 100 ms` (tab was backgrounded). `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` kills, in order: the CRT flicker, the boil (static mean field only), the screen shake, the freeze frames, the odometer roll, the hull burn, and the marching ants. The game remains fully playable and fully legible — the dither field alone carries the information. --- ## 11. WHAT THIS DESIGN DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO (for the «Известные ограничения» section) - The realities count is **exact only below ~10⁴**; above that it is a sampled estimate and the UI says so with a tilde. Faking precision would be the one lie this game cannot afford. - Ghost samples are drawn from a bounded pool (256). At the very start the pool is a vanishingly small slice of the true space — the boil is *representative*, not exhaustive, and the README must say it in one sentence. - No audio on iOS Safari before the first gesture, by design; the start button is the gate and there is no autoplay fallback. ### Critical Files for Implementation - G:\Другие компьютеры\PAULEKMAN\dev\nostromo-gambit\public\theme.css - G:\Другие компьютеры\PAULEKMAN\dev\nostromo-gambit\public\sprites.js - G:\Другие компьютеры\PAULEKMAN\dev\nostromo-gambit\public\board.js - G:\Другие компьютеры\PAULEKMAN\dev\nostromo-gambit\public\app.js - G:\Другие компьютеры\PAULEKMAN\dev\nostromo-gambit\public\index.html New files this direction requires (to be created in `C:\dev\\public\`): `render.mjs` (the single rAF loop, dither tiles, ghost slots, FX queue), `ghosts.mjs` (sample pool + RLE decode), `audio.mjs` (synth engine, collapse-driven music bus), `counter.mjs` (odometer + collapse beat), alongside a `theme.css` / `sprites.js` / `index.html` derived from the five files above.

# CONTRARIAN REVIEW: kill the obvious design, then rebuild it

## 1. Stress test of "8-bit Battleship with a legally-cheating defender"

I played it out. It fails, and not in a fixable-with-tuning way.

**Failure 1 — the 50-miss opening.** On 10×10 with the classic fleet (20 ship cells, no-touch rule), an adversarial defender answers МИМО for as long as the un-shot cells can still pack the fleet. That is roughly 45–60 shots. The literal first two thirds of the game is: click, «МИМО», click, «МИМО». The counter drops 10¹⁶ → 10¹² and the player feels nothing, because both numbers are "unimaginably many". Then packing goes tight and the last 20 shots are a forced avalanche the player did not cause. That is not a difficulty curve, it is a cliff with a corridor in front of it.

**Failure 2 — during the miss-run every shot is equally good, so there is no decision.** The only real decision is the *shape* of the shot set, and there is essentially one right shape (a dense blocking cluster / lattice that kills packing fastest). Player who finds it plays the identical opening forever; player who doesn't plays noise.

**Failure 3 — it deletes the only fun loop Battleship has.** Battleship's pleasure is hit → hunt → kill. An adversary that may re-place the fleet around your hit destroys hunt mode entirely: you hit, and next turn the ship is somewhere else. You are left with a coin-flip clicker. This is exactly the prompt's suspicion, and it is worse than suspected — good play is not merely unrewarded, the *reward structure itself is removed*.

**Failure 4 — «УБИЛ» becomes almost unreachable.** A kill requires every surviving reality to agree the ship is fully struck. Mid-game therefore delivers hits with no kills: reads as "the game is cheating and never paying out."

**Failure 5 — the counter cannot be honest.** Counting consistent full-fleet placements on 10×10 is #P-hard territory; you would ship a Monte-Carlo estimate rendered as a precise integer. That is a *fake precise number*, and it is the single most off-brand thing this project could do. nostromo-gambit's entire personality is «честный отказ лучше подделанного десанта» — Fischer castling disabled and admitted on the start screen, a failed drop refunding the die and printing the reason. A lying counter as the centrepiece would poison the whole thing.

**Failure 6 — the two headline power-ups are anti-mechanics.** "The machine does your evasion for you" is not a choice, it is a button. And a Geller field that pins a region is a resource you spend to *turn the interesting mechanic off* — optimal play is to disable the game.

Verdict: the obvious design is a spreadsheet in a beautiful CRT costume. Reject it at 10×10 Battleship scale.

## 2. What the seed actually contains that is worth keeping

- **Unobserved = unfixed = hostile.** Lovecraft framing is the best line in the brainstorm.
- **A shot lands in all branches at once**; a munition that covers several branches.
- **Ghost fleets converging** — genuinely gorgeous, genuinely cheap to render.
- **Pinning reality** («пришпилить») as a verb.
- The friend's instinct about *knights and liars* — logic-puzzle DNA.

The fatal ingredient is not the concept. It is **the scale**. At 10×10 the mechanic is uncountable, unreadable and unplayable. At 8×8 with 3–5 ships it becomes *exactly computable in milliseconds*, the counter becomes a small honest number you can feel, and every action moves it legibly.

## 3. RECOMMENDATION — commit to this

### «CARCOSA ECHO» · ГЛУБОКОВОДНЫЙ ПРОМЕР · ПРОТОКОЛ ПРИШПИЛИВАНИЯ
*(title swappable; the shape "English proper noun + term, Russian subtitle" matches NOSTROMO GAMBIT)*

A turn-based **deduction duel**, structured as a **roguelike dive of 7 short encounters**. You are not shooting at a hidden fleet. You are **interrogating an entity that must always answer truthfully but is free to re-choose which truth was always true, everywhere you have not nailed reality down.**

**The thesis, and the win condition: knowledge, not damage.** You win an encounter when the number of realities consistent with your evidence reaches **1**. You do not have to sink the fleet — you have to *know* it. Once it is known in every reality, it is real, and the surface guns finish it. This single rule is what makes the counter a health bar instead of a progress bar, promotes non-shooting verbs to first class, and is a thing no Battleship variant has ever done.

**Board & fleet.** 8×8 / 3 ships (4,3,2) at depth 1, escalating to 10×10 / 5 ships at depth 7. Russian no-touch rule. Sizes are chosen so the possibility set is **exactly enumerable** (bitboard DP over per-ship placement sets), giving exact count, exact per-cell marginals and exact uniform sampling. **No estimate is ever shown as a fact.**

**The two laws (printed in the UI, never violated):**
1. **ОН НЕ ЛЖЁТ.** Every answer ever given stays true of every surviving reality.
2. **ГВОЗДЬ ДЕРЖИТ.** A confirmed **hit is a permanent pin** — no reweave may ever vacate that cell. Hits accumulate into a skeleton that strangles the god. This restores hunt mode *and* is the literal fictional statement of the seed: he twists reality only where you have not nailed it.

**And the counter-pressure, which is what turns it from spreadsheet to game:** **misses rot.** A МИМО is a weak mark that decays after ~6 turns and is then reclaimed by the drift — the god may put a ship there again, and the counter goes **UP**, in amber. Hits are eternal; knowledge is perishable. The counter oscillates (40 000 → 900 → 3 100 → 400) and the encounter is a race, not a grind.

**Four verbs — each a different *shape of question*:**

| verb | air | effect |
|---|---|---|
| **ПРОМЕР** | 1 | Point a cell. ПОПАЛ (permanent nail) / МИМО (decaying mark) / УБИЛ. |
| **ВЕЕР** | 2 | Name a row/column/diagonal. The god must answer the exact **count** of ship cells on it — choosing the most convenient surviving reality. |
| **ГВОЗДЬ** | 3 | Freeze a 2×2. The god must **commit** to that region's contents forever — and does **not** tell you what it committed. You read the answer off the **counter's drop**: 8 400 → 900 means it was full; 8 400 → 8 100 means empty. |
| **ЗАЛП ПО ВЕТВЯМ** | 5, limited ammo | Fire into the possibility space: delete every reality where the target cell is empty. Guaranteed hit — unless no reality has a ship there, in which case: «ЗАЛП В ПУСТОТУ», you lose the ammo and the air. |

The central human skill this creates: **ask questions where every answer hurts him.** That is real, deep, non-automatable skill (adversarial 20-questions / Mastermind DNA), and it is *not* solved by displaying the counter, because the choice is about the shape of the partition, not its size. Note that ГВОЗДЬ makes the reality counter a **measuring instrument** — that is the fix for failure 2, and it is the reason to keep the counter at all.

**The god's clock — «СМЕЩЕНИЕ» (drift).** Reweaving costs drift; drift regenerates +1/turn. At zero, the brane **freezes** and the HUD says so in amber: «БРАНА ЗАСТЫЛА · 1 ХОД». Now the player has tempo: bait him into burning drift, then strike during the freeze. This is what converts an unbeatable optimiser into an opponent with a readable rhythm — visible on the HUD, not a hidden AI handicap.

**The faces — doctrine, not optimality.** Personality-as-data, exactly like `src/game/storytellers.mjs` (a weights table + a `tone: {start,done,skipped}` triple). ХОЛОДНЫЙ (greedy max-realities, the teacher) · ПРЯДИЛЬЩИК (prefers mirror-symmetric realities — info on one half transfers to the other) · ГОЛОДНЫЙ (drifts toward you, accepting worse counts — the centre empties) · СКУПОЙ (hoards drift, then one huge shift) · and the boss **КОРОЛЬ В ЖЁЛТОМ**, actually optimal, who once per encounter may **pull out one of your nails** — the only violation of the game's own law, announced with the whole screen tearing. Each doctrine is printed honestly on the pre-dive card. **There is deliberately no lying face**, and the docs must say why: break the truth invariant once and every deduction in the game becomes worthless.

**Visual signature.** Per-cell marginals (a free byproduct of the exact DP) render as an **amber possibility fog**; 24 uniformly-sampled realities are stroked as 1px ghost hulls at ~12% opacity. As the count collapses the fog condenses into solid hulls; at count = 1 the fleet snaps solid with a shockwave. Nails are hard green rivets. Marks visibly fade with a `●●●○○` decay readout (reuse the reference's `.pips` idiom). The reweave is a **200 ms horizontal-scanline displacement glitch** — the brane crossing. The counter is a mechanical split-flap digit roll, green falling / amber rising, with `−7 411` / `+1 902` under it.

**Audio — where this exceeds the bar.** The reference has none. Hand-written WebAudio, zero assets, created on the start-screen gesture, toggle in the drawer: sonar ping with a delayed return; noise wash for МИМО; square thunk + detuned metallic ring for ПОПАЛ; 5-note descent for УБИЛ; ring-modulated pitch-swept noise burst for the reweave; and — the idea worth having — **a sustained low drone that plays exactly while the brane is frozen**, i.e. a sound that carries state. Green = clean waveforms, amber = noise/ring-mod, one alert timbre. Ambient bass gains a voice per depth: free escalation feedback.

**Architecture — drop the server.** nostromo-gambit needed one only because Stockfish is a native GPL process. Here the solver is a few hundred lines of pure JS over bitboards, <10 ms per query. Keeping the server would be cargo cult. Ship it **single-page, zero-dependency, publishable as an Artifact** — a real ergonomic upgrade the brief itself flags. Keep the reference's best instinct (an authoritative model the view never second-guesses) by putting the possibility engine in a **Web Worker**, inlined as a Blob URL so single-file publishing survives. Regain reload-resume with one localStorage slot, and say in REPORT.md that this tradeoff flipped relative to the reference project and why.

**The honesty clause (write it into the UI and both docs).** The exact counter is guaranteed only up to the shipped board/fleet sizes, verified by a bench script measuring worst-case count time. Configurations that would exceed the budget **are not shipped** — the game never silently degrades to an estimate.

### What I am willing to lose
- **10×10 and the classic fleet.** The classic scale is precisely what makes the mechanic uncountable and unplayable. Non-negotiable.
- **The player's own defended fleet / the symmetric duel.** Doubles the systems, halves the polish, and the defensive half is passive. Preserved as one late run-card, «ОТРАЖЕНИЕ», that lets you reweave *his* fleet once — a delicious moment instead of a whole mode.
- **The "14 000 605" fantasy number.** Trading a big impressive lie for a small honest one; the Doctor Strange beat is honoured better by *showing all remaining realities at once* at the end.
- **Server, SSE, optimistic concurrency, multi-tab.** Bought with an Artifact link the user can open on his phone.
- **Stockfish-grade opponent depth.** A perfect optimiser is both incomputable at scale and unfun at any scale.

### Honest risks in MY design
1. It is cerebral; Battleship expectations will be violated. Mitigated by short encounters, the fog's readability, the audio drama, and ЗАЛП as the big dumb gun.
2. ВЕЕР's exact count may be too strong and trivialise encounters — must be balanced empirically.
3. Mark decay can read as cheating. Mitigated by making decay fully visible and never retroactive on hits, plus a run card that slows it.
4. Max-Δ shooting is partially a solved optimisation. Accepted: ГВОЗДЬ and ВЕЕР branch on the *answer*, which Δ does not capture. **Never ship a best-move hint.** Say so in the README.
5. Mitigation infrastructure is mandatory, copying the reference's «главный оракул»: a headless **selfplay harness** playing N runs with invariants asserted on every action — (a) truth: every answer ever given remains satisfiable; (b) monotonic: nails never vacate; (c) solvability: no encounter is unwinnable at start; (d) curve: distribution of actions-to-win per depth stays in band. That script is what makes this a finished product rather than a prototype.

**Scope to hit the bar (~6 100 runtime lines / ~8 900 total / two Russian docs with «Известные ограничения»):** possibility engine ~600 · faces ~350 · encounter state machine + verbs ~450 · run layer + cards ~300 · `rng.mjs` lifted verbatim 76 · audio ~400 · sprites ~450 · board+fog view ~350 · app/HUD/screens ~700 · theme.css ~700 · worker bridge ~150 · tests ~1 500 (the engine is pure, so it tests *better* than the reference's engine-coupled tier) · selfplay+bench ~500 · docs ~350.

# ГАМБИТ ЛЕВИАФАНА — нарративный проект

## 1. Премиса (три предложения)

Вы — офицер огневого решения разведывательного корвета «ЛОТ», последнего корабля, который ещё держит связь с нашей версией мира, и вы охотитесь на флот, ушедший за брану: их корпуса несут двигатели Алькубьерре, которые не умеют ходить во времени, но умеют переложить корабль в соседнюю реальность, где он стоял иначе.

Поэтому вражеский флот не спрятан — он **не определён**: он существует сразу во всех расстановках, которые не противоречат тому, что уже было сказано вслух.

А сказанное вслух держится потому, что выстрел настоящий: снаряд приходит одновременно во все ветви, и вода обязана ответить — мимо, шрам или киль; этот ответ выжигается в бране как рубец, и Левиафан волен переложить флот в любую реальность, согласную со всеми рубцами, но не в ту, что хоть одному из них противоречит.

**Осевая строка всего проекта:**
> ЛЕВИАФАН НЕ ЛЖЁТ. ЛЕВИАФАН ПЕРЕКЛАДЫВАЕТ ТО, О ЧЁМ ВЫ НЕ СПРОСИЛИ.

Это одновременно логлайн, подзаголовок, и обещание игроку: правила честные, обманывает вас не код, а недостаток ваших вопросов.

## 4. Тёмный бог действует

Левиафан — не декорация и не второй игрок. Второй игрок — это **флот** (перекладка + ответные залпы). Левиафан — это то, что просыпается, когда вы слишком долго держитесь за мультивселенную.

**Шкала: ГЛУБИНА, в саженях. 0…30.**
Растёт: +1 за каждую вашу перекладку; +1 за каждую перекладку врага, случившуюся при вашем открытом (не закессоненном) поле; +2 за каждый киль в третьем акте («вода помнит»). Падает: −1 за каждый поставленный кессон (единственный способ всплыть — пришпиливать реальность).

На саженях 8, 14, 20, 25 и 29 бросается **ИСКАЖЕНИЕ**. Таблица (детерминированно, через `Rng.fork('leviathan')`):

| Искажение | Механика | Строка в журнале |
|---|---|---|
| **ПОДМЕНА** | Один ваш корпус перекладывается без вашего согласия. Какой — не сообщается | `ВАШ СТРОЙ ИЗМЕНИЛСЯ. ВАМ НЕ СКАЗАЛИ, ГДЕ.` |
| **СЛЕПОЕ ПЯТНО** | Один случайный старый шрам стирается из протокола. Ветви, которые он отсекал, возвращаются. Счётчик согласных ветвей **растёт** | `РУБЕЦ ЗАЛИЗАН. ВЫ БОЛЬШЕ НЕ ЗНАЕТЕ ТОГО, ЧТО ЗНАЛИ.` |
| **ЛОЖНЫЙ КИЛЬ** | На 3 хода теневой строй показывает несогласные образцы. Приборы врут, игра об этом честно предупреждает | `ТЕНЕВОЙ СТРОЙ НЕ ЗАСЛУЖИВАЕТ ДОВЕРИЯ. 3 ХОДА.` |
| **ПРИЛИВ** (только акт III) | Один потопленный корпус возвращается в воду с полным здоровьем в любую согласную клетку | `ЛЕВИАФАН ВЫДОХНУЛ. ОДИН КОРПУС ВЕРНУЛСЯ.` |
| **ИМЯ** | Левиафан обращается к вам по званию, потом по фамилии. Кессон стоит два хода вместо одного, 4 хода | `ОНО НАЗВАЛО ВАС ПО ИМЕНИ. КЕССОН ПОДОРОЖАЛ.` |

**Сажень 30 — отдельное поражение.** Не «вас потопили», а «вас забрали». Отдельный экран, отдельный текст (§6).

Почему это работает: игрок сам выбирает, насколько сильно опираться на мультивселенную, и цена не абстрактная — она бьёт ровно по тому, чем он пользовался. Он врал в рамках правил — теперь врут его приборы.
